questions.stem: In a histologic study of an implantation site about 2 weeks after fertilization, a population of fetal-derived cells is found that secretes enzymes easing the burrowing of the overlying cell layer into the endometrium, continually supplies new cells that relocate into that overlying layer, and forms columns that invade maternal arteries. Which of the following cell populations is being described?

explanation.summary: The cytotrophoblast (inner trophoblast layer) makes invasion enzymes, feeds new cells to the syncytiotrophoblast, and forms columns that invade maternal arteries.
explanation.whyCorrect: The trophoblast has an outer syncytiotrophoblast and an inner cytotrophoblast. The cytotrophoblast produces enzymes that help the syncytiotrophoblast burrow into the endometrium, is a source of new cells that relocate to the syncytiotrophoblast, and forms columns that invade maternal arteries to establish the uteroplacental circulation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Decidual cells are maternal, progesterone-modified endometrium, not fetal cells that invade maternal arteries.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These maternal NK cells regulate invasion depth and spiral artery remodeling but are not fetal-derived and do not become syncytium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myometrium is the maternal tissue invaded (inner third); it does not supply trophoblast cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The syncytiotrophoblast is the outer layer that does the burrowing and receives new cells; it is not the source of the enzymes and relocating cells.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation has a blood pressure of 166/110 mm Hg, 3+ proteinuria, elevated serum transaminases, and a rising serum creatinine. Her blood pressure was normal before 20 weeks. A defect in which of the following early pregnancy processes most likely underlies her condition?

choices.label: B
choices.text: hCG rescue of the corpus luteum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast invasion of the uterine wall

explanation.summary: Preeclampsia is caused by faulty trophoblast implantation into the uterine wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preeclampsia (hypertension with endothelial dysfunction, usually after 20 weeks) results from faulty implantation of the trophoblast in the uterine wall. The improper implantation disrupts placental blood flow and triggers systemic inflammation, producing maternal organ dysfunction such as liver and kidney damage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fas ligand protects the fetus by inducing maternal T-cell apoptosis; it is not the lesion in preeclampsia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Failed luteal rescue would cause loss of progesterone support early in pregnancy, not preeclampsia after 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hPL alters maternal glucose and lipid metabolism; it is not the cause of preeclampsia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Failure to shed the zona pellucida would prevent implantation altogether rather than cause late-onset hypertension.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has a positive pregnancy test 4 weeks after her last menstrual period. In a nonconception cycle, the declining luteal stimulation late in the cycle would allow her corpus luteum to shrink and sex hormone levels to fall. Which of the following hormones prevents this and keeps the corpus luteum secreting progesterone?

explanation.summary: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast rescues the corpus luteum so it keeps making progesterone, estrogen, and relaxin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Late in the cycle LH is insufficient to maintain the corpus luteum. After implantation, hCG secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast stimulates the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone, estrogen, and relaxin during the first 10 weeks of pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Placental CRH stimulates prostaglandins and DHEA to help induce contractions at term.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen is secreted by the corpus luteum under hCG stimulation; it is not the rescuing signal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hPL alters maternal metabolism to supply the fetus; it does not act on luteal cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin is itself a product of the corpus luteum early in pregnancy; it does not sustain the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 15 weeks' gestation undergoes removal of the ovary containing the corpus luteum because of torsion. She receives no hormone supplementation, and the pregnancy continues without complication. Which of the following best explains the maintenance of her progesterone levels?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placental lactogen now substitutes for it

explanation.summary: After about 10 weeks the syncytiotrophoblast makes progesterone and estrogen, so the corpus luteum is no longer needed.
explanation.whyCorrect: hCG-driven corpus luteum production of progesterone is temporary. After 10 weeks, progesterone and estrogen are produced by placental syncytiotrophoblast cells (and relaxin by cytotrophoblasts), so loss of the corpus luteum at 15 weeks does not end the pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: After week 10 cytotrophoblasts produce relaxin; progesterone and estrogen come from the syncytiotrophoblast.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The decidua is endometrium modified by progesterone; it is not the placental source of progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hPL alters maternal metabolism and does not replace progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Relaxin only assists progesterone in placental growth; it does not replace progesterone.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 26 weeks' gestation has a mildly elevated postprandial glucose level. A hormone synthesized by the syncytiotrophoblast is contributing by raising maternal glucose, lowering maternal glucose utilization, and increasing lipolysis so that the fetus is assured adequate nutrition. Which of the following hormones is responsible?

explanation.summary: Human placental lactogen raises maternal glucose, reduces maternal glucose use, and increases lipolysis to secure fetal nutrition.
explanation.whyCorrect: Human placental lactogen is made by the syncytiotrophoblast. It ensures adequate fetal nutrition by altering maternal metabolism: increasing glucose levels, lowering glucose utilization, and increasing lipolysis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CRH stimulates prostaglandins and DHEA to promote contractions at term.
whyWrongByChoice.B: hCG maintains the corpus luteum through the LH receptor; its described role is not metabolic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone is the principal driver of placental growth; it is not described as shifting maternal fuel use.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Relaxin assists progesterone in placental growth and is made by cytotrophoblasts after week 10.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation asks how the sugar from her meals reaches her baby. The fetus relies on this sugar as its primary energy source. By which mechanism does it cross the placenta?

explanation.summary: Glucose, the main fetal energy source, crosses the placenta by facilitated diffusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glucose moves by facilitated diffusion: passive movement down a concentration gradient via a pore or channel. It is the primary energy source for the fetus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Active transport is used for amino acids, water-soluble vitamins, calcium, iron, iodine, and phosphate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fc receptor transport is the special route for maternal IgG after endocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Receptor-mediated endocytosis moves fatty acids, LDL cholesterol, and IgG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Simple/passive diffusion is used for gases, water, sodium, fat-soluble vitamins, and waste products.

questions.stem: A medical student reviewing placental transport notes that some nutrients require energy expenditure to cross the membrane. Which of the following crosses the placenta by active transport?

explanation.summary: Amino acids cross the placenta by active transport.
explanation.whyCorrect: Active transport, movement across a membrane that requires energy, is used for amino acids as well as water-soluble vitamins, calcium, iron, iodine, and phosphate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fatty acids cross by receptor-mediated endocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucose crosses by facilitated diffusion, a passive process.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxygen crosses by passive diffusion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium crosses by passive diffusion.

questions.stem: In the placenta, carbon dioxide diffuses from fetal red blood cells into the maternal circulation, where it is later removed by the maternal lungs. Which of the following best describes how this carbon dioxide movement promotes oxygen uptake by the fetus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal blood acidifies, raising fetal hemoglobin O2 affinity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetal blood alkalinizes, lowering fetal hemoglobin O2 affinity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fetal blood alkalinizes, raising fetal hemoglobin O2 affinity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maternal blood acidifies, raising maternal hemoglobin O2 affinity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maternal blood alkalinizes, raising maternal hemoglobin O2 affinity

explanation.summary: CO2 leaving fetal blood makes it alkaline, raising fetal hemoglobin's O2 affinity (double Bohr effect).
explanation.whyCorrect: As CO2 diffuses from fetus to mother, maternal blood becomes more acidic and fetal blood more alkaline. The alkaline pH increases the affinity of fetal hemoglobin for oxygen, while the acidic maternal pH lowers maternal hemoglobin affinity (Bohr effect), both promoting fetal O2 uptake.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal blood loses CO2 and becomes more alkaline, not acidic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An alkaline pH increases hemoglobin O2 affinity (Bohr effect).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acidification lowers, not raises, maternal hemoglobin O2 affinity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Maternal blood gains CO2 and becomes more acidic; higher maternal affinity would hinder O2 release.

questions.stem: Trophoblast cells in contact with maternal blood express an atypical cell-surface human lymphocyte antigen rather than the usual antigens. Its interaction with maternal natural killer cells and cytotoxic T cells makes them more tolerant of the fetus. Which molecule is expressed?

explanation.summary: Trophoblast HLA-G makes maternal NK cells and cytotoxic T cells tolerant of the fetus.
explanation.whyCorrect: HLAs are usually HLA-A or HLA-B antigens. The trophoblast expresses atypical HLA-G, which interacts with maternal NK cells and cytotoxic T cells when in contact with maternal blood, making them more tolerant of the fetus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Fas receptor is on maternal lymphocytes; the trophoblast expresses Fas ligand.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intracellular Fc receptors in the syncytiotrophoblast transport maternal IgG; they are not HLA molecules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA-A is one of the usual antigens used to distinguish self from non-self, not the atypical trophoblast antigen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA-B is one of the usual antigens; the trophoblast instead expresses atypical HLA-G.

questions.stem: In an experimental model, a drug blocks a placental enzyme that is present from about day 6 after fertilization and normally deprives maternal T cells of a nutrient they need for survival. Local concentration of which of the following substances would most likely increase?

explanation.summary: Placental IDO degrades tryptophan to kynurenine; blocking it raises tryptophan and supports maternal T cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase breaks down tryptophan into kynurenine and is present from day 6. Maternal T cells need tryptophan to survive, so IDO protects the fetus by depleting it; kynurenine also inhibits T-cell development. Inhibiting IDO would increase local tryptophan.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DHEA is raised by placental CRH near term, not by this enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fas ligand is a trophoblast surface protein unrelated to this enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kynurenine is the product of IDO; blocking the enzyme lowers, not raises, kynurenine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Relaxin is a hormone from the corpus luteum and later cytotrophoblasts, not an IDO substrate.

questions.stem: Maternal T lymphocytes that come into direct contact with trophoblast cells undergo programmed cell death after a receptor-ligand interaction, reducing the chance that they target the fetus. Which of the following interactions is responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maternal Fas ligand with trophoblast Fas receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maternal IgG with syncytiotrophoblast Fc receptors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trophoblast Fas ligand with maternal Fas receptor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trophoblast HLA-A with maternal cytotoxic T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trophoblast HLA-G with maternal NK cell receptors

explanation.summary: Trophoblast Fas ligand binds Fas receptor on maternal lymphocytes, triggering their apoptosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trophoblast cells express Fas ligand, which interacts with the Fas receptor on maternal lymphocytes. After this interaction, maternal T lymphocytes undergo apoptosis, lowering the likelihood of an attack on the fetus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The direction is reversed; the ligand is on the trophoblast and the receptor on maternal lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fc receptors transport maternal IgG to the fetus; this does not kill maternal lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA-A is a usual self/non-self antigen; the trophoblast expresses atypical HLA-G instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA-G makes maternal NK and T cells tolerant; it is not described as inducing apoptosis.

questions.stem: Cord blood from a healthy term newborn contains high levels of maternal-derived antibody that will protect the infant for several months. These are large molecules that cannot pass freely through the placental barrier. How did they reach the fetal circulation?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leakage through breaks in chorionic villi

explanation.summary: Maternal IgG is endocytosed by the syncytiotrophoblast and carried to the fetal side on intracellular Fc receptors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Large IgG molecules cross via the syncytiotrophoblast by a unique mechanism: they are first taken up by endocytosis and then bind intracellular Fc receptors that transport them to the fetal side. This occurs during the last trimester and gives passive immunity lasting several months.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Active transport is used for amino acids and some minerals and vitamins, not IgG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Facilitated diffusion via channels is the route for glucose, not IgG.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The placenta maintains a barrier between maternal and fetal cells; IgG uses a specific mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Large IgG molecules do not diffuse passively; they are taken up by the syncytiotrophoblast.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman comes for her first prenatal visit. The first day of her last menstrual period was exactly 10 weeks ago. She has regular 28-day cycles, and she believes conception occurred about 2 weeks after that date. Which gestational age should be documented in her chart?

explanation.summary: Gestational age is counted in completed weeks from the first day of the LMP, not from conception.
explanation.whyCorrect: By convention, gestational age is expressed in completed weeks from the first day of the last menstrual period. Because ovulation and conception occur about 2 weeks after the LMP, the fertilization age is roughly 2 weeks less than the gestational age; this is why the estimated delivery date at 40 weeks corresponds to about 38 weeks of in utero life.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 8 weeks is the approximate fertilization (conception) age, not the conventionally documented gestational age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 9 weeks has no basis; gestational age is dated from the first day of the LMP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 11 weeks overestimates; exactly 10 weeks have passed since the first day of the LMP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 12 weeks would add 2 weeks rather than dating from the LMP itself.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman learns she is pregnant after taking a medication with known teratogenic potential throughout the past month. Her gestational age is 6 weeks. Exposure at this point in pregnancy carries the greatest risk of congenital anomalies chiefly because it coincides with which process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attainment of fetal viability outside the uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Development of most embryonic organ systems

choices.label: C
choices.text: Final maturation of the fetal lungs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quickening and rapid gain in fetal weight

explanation.summary: Toxic exposures in the first trimester (embryonic period) are most likely to cause congenital abnormalities because most organ systems form then.
explanation.whyCorrect: The first trimester includes the embryonic period (fertilization weeks 3-8), during which most of the organ systems develop. Therefore toxic exposures at this time are the most likely to produce congenital abnormalities; the fetal period begins in week 9 and continues to delivery.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Viability is reached at 22-24 weeks, well after this exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal lung maturity is not typically complete until about 36 weeks, in the third trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The placenta takes over progesterone production at about 10 weeks; this is not what makes early exposures teratogenic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Quickening is first perceived at about 20 weeks, in the second trimester.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman plans to conceive in the next few months. She has no personal or family history of neural tube defects and takes no chronic medications. Which folic acid regimen is recommended for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 400 μg daily, from at least 1 month preconception to end of first trimester

choices.label: B
choices.text: 400 μg daily, starting at the 18-20 week fetal anatomy ultrasound examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: 400 μg daily, starting once pregnancy is confirmed and continuing to delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Higher-dose daily, from 3 months preconception and continuing through delivery

choices.label: E
choices.text: None needed, provided a prenatal vitamin is begun at 12 weeks of gestation

explanation.summary: Average-risk patients should take 400 μg folic acid daily from at least 1 month before conception through the end of the first trimester.
explanation.whyCorrect: The neural tube closes about 28 days after conception, often before a patient realizes she is pregnant. To lower NTD risk, those planning pregnancy are advised to take 400 μg of folic acid daily beginning at least 1 month before conception and continuing until the end of the first trimester. Higher doses for longer durations are reserved for high-risk patients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: By 18-20 weeks neural tube closure is long complete, so starting then gives no NTD protection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Starting at confirmation of pregnancy is too late; the neural tube may already have closed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Higher-dose, longer regimens are for high-risk patients (prior NTD, anti-seizure drugs, strong family history), which she is not.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting until 12 weeks misses the preconception and early-embryonic window when folate prevents NTDs.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman at 17 weeks' gestation undergoes a quad screen. Results show decreased alpha-fetoprotein, decreased estriol, increased hCG, and increased inhibin A. This pattern is most consistent with which fetal condition?

explanation.summary: Quad screen in trisomy 21: low AFP, low estriol, high hCG, high inhibin A.
explanation.whyCorrect: The quad screen (15-22 weeks) measures AFP, hCG, estriol and inhibin A in maternal serum to estimate aneuploidy risk. Trisomy 21 classically shows decreased AFP and estriol with increased hCG and inhibin A.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anencephaly is an open neural tube defect, which elevates rather than lowers AFP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cystic fibrosis is evaluated by carrier screening of the parents, not by quad screen markers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Open neural tube defects raise AFP; this patient's AFP is decreased.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trisomy 18 shows decreases in all markers, including hCG, rather than elevated hCG and inhibin A.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman at 12 weeks' gestation has a cell-free DNA test reported as high risk for trisomy 21. She wants a definitive answer as early in pregnancy as possible. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat cell-free DNA testing in 4 weeks

explanation.summary: A positive cfDNA screen requires diagnostic confirmation; at 10-13 weeks the diagnostic option is CVS.
explanation.whyCorrect: cfDNA is a screening test; a high-risk result requires confirmation with diagnostic (or postnatal) testing. Chorionic villus sampling is performed at 10-13 weeks and uses an ultrasound-guided needle to obtain placental tissue for direct genetic analysis, so it gives the earliest definitive answer at 12 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniocentesis is diagnostic but is performed at 15-22 weeks, not at 12 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carrier screening detects parental single-gene carrier status (eg, CF, SMA), not fetal aneuploidy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The quad screen is another screening test and is now largely replaced by cfDNA; it cannot confirm aneuploidy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Repeating a screening test does not provide a diagnosis; a positive screen should prompt diagnostic testing.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation by an early dating ultrasound is seen for a routine visit. The pregnancy is progressing normally. On abdominal examination, where is the uterine fundus expected to be palpated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the level of the maternal umbilicus

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the level of the xiphoid process

choices.label: D
choices.text: Midway between the umbilicus and xiphoid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Still contained within the bony pelvis

explanation.summary: At 20 weeks the fundus reaches the umbilicus, and fundal height (cm) approximately equals gestational weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the second trimester the uterus expands into the abdomen, and at 20 weeks the fundus is at the level of the maternal umbilicus. Fundal height, measured from the symphysis pubis to the fundus, should be about 20 cm at 20 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A fundus at the xiphoid would indicate a far more advanced pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The uterus becomes just palpable above the pubic symphysis at about 12 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fundus above the umbilicus would be expected later than 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The uterus stays within the bony pelvis only in the first trimester.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 26 weeks' gestation has a venous glucose level measured 1 hour after drinking a 50-gram glucose solution. The result is elevated. She has no polyuria or polydipsia. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diagnose GDM and start dietary therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain a fasting urine glucose level

explanation.summary: An elevated 1-hour 50-g screen is followed by a 100-g 3-hour GTT; GDM is diagnosed only if that is also elevated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Between 24 and 28 weeks, patients are screened for GDM with a 1-hour venous glucose after a 50-g oral load. If elevated, a 100-g 3-hour glucose tolerance test follows, and an elevated result on that test meets criteria for GDM.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Treatment is premature; the screening result has not yet been confirmed by the diagnostic 3-hour test.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An elevated 1-hour screen alone does not meet criteria for GDM.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urine glucose is not part of the described two-step GDM testing sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delaying to repeat the screen postpones diagnosis; the next step is the 100-g 3-hour test.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman, G2P1, is seen at 28 weeks' gestation. Her blood type is O, RhD-negative. An indirect Coombs test in the first trimester was negative, and a repeat indirect Coombs test today is again negative for anti-D antibodies. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amniocentesis to determine fetal RhD status

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct Coombs test on maternal red cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serial ultrasound surveillance for fetal anemia

explanation.summary: RhD-negative patients with a negative antibody screen receive RhoGAM at 28 weeks to prevent anti-D formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: RhD-negative patients have an indirect Coombs test in the first trimester and again in the late second trimester. If the antibody screen remains negative, RhoGAM is given at 28 weeks to block the patient from forming anti-D antibodies, protecting future pregnancies.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Invasive fetal testing is not part of routine management of an unsensitized RhD-negative patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The indirect Coombs test detects circulating maternal antibodies; a direct Coombs on maternal cells adds nothing here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Withholding prophylaxis leaves her at risk of sensitization; RhoGAM is indicated at 28 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serial ultrasound for fetal anemia is indicated when anti-D antibodies are present at elevated titers, not when the screen is negative.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 36 weeks' gestation has a rectovaginal swab that grows Streptococcus agalactiae. She has no symptoms and no drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No treatment, as colonization is harmless

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral amoxicillin now, then repeat the swab

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat her partner and rescreen at 38 weeks

explanation.summary: GBS-positive patients receive intrapartum antibiotics (penicillin), cutting neonatal infection by about 80%.
explanation.whyCorrect: ACOG recommends universal GBS screening at 36 to 37 6/7 weeks by rectovaginal swab. Patients who screen positive are treated during labor with antibiotics (penicillin unless allergy requires an alternative), which reduces neonatal infection by approximately 80%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Although colonization is harmless to her, GBS can cause neonatal septicemia and pneumonia, so intrapartum treatment is indicated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Treating before labor is not recommended because colonization is transient and likely to recur before delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cesarean delivery is not the described strategy; intrapartum antibiotics are.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Partner treatment and rescreening are not part of the recommended approach.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus at 27 weeks' gestation. Her glucose control over the next several weeks is poor. Her first-trimester course was uncomplicated. Which of the following is her newborn most at risk of developing?

explanation.summary: GDM causes fetal hyperinsulinemia and neonatal hypoglycemia, but not major malformations, because hyperglycemia begins after organogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Maternal glucose crosses the placenta, and the fetus responds with hyperinsulinemia. GDM therefore raises the risk of macrosomia, fetal hyperinsulinemia with neonatal hypoglycemia, and neonatal respiratory distress. Unlike pregestational diabetes, GDM is not typically associated with major congenital malformations because the hyperglycemia occurs after organogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neural tube defects arise from failed closure about 28 days after conception, long before GDM develops.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Major congenital malformations are associated with pregestational diabetes, not GDM arising after organogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal hemolytic anemia results from maternal anti-D antibodies, not maternal hyperglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neonatal pertussis risk relates to lack of passive immunity (addressed by maternal Tdap), not GDM.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 8 weeks' gestation reports daily nausea and occasional vomiting, worst in the mornings. She asks which hormone is responsible. Rising levels of which hormone correlate with these symptoms?

explanation.summary: High beta-hCG levels from the placenta correlate with nausea and vomiting of early pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: beta-hCG is a glycoprotein hormone released by the placenta a few days after implantation. Its high levels in early pregnancy are likely directly or indirectly responsible for nausea and vomiting, which typically recede in the second trimester as beta-hCG levels off.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AFP is produced by the fetal liver and is used to screen for NTDs and aneuploidy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estriol is a quad screen marker, not the hormone linked to early-pregnancy nausea.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibin A is a quad screen marker, not the hormone linked to early-pregnancy nausea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Progesterone supports the endometrium (taken over by the placenta at about 10 weeks) but is not the hormone correlated with morning sickness.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation received a low-risk cell-free DNA result for common aneuploidies. Her cousin was born with spina bifida, and she asks whether this result means her fetus does not have a neural tube defect. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not evaluate NTD risk; maternal serum screening can

choices.label: B
choices.text: It estimates NTD risk only when combined with carrier screening

choices.label: C
choices.text: It must be confirmed with CVS before NTDs can be excluded

choices.label: D
choices.text: It rules out open NTDs with high sensitivity and specificity

choices.label: E
choices.text: NTDs can be evaluated only by examination after delivery

explanation.summary: cfDNA screens for common aneuploidies but does not assess NTD risk; serum screening (AFP) +/- NT estimates NTD risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Non-invasive prenatal testing with cfDNA sequences placental DNA fragments in maternal blood to detect common aneuploidies, but it does not assess neural tube defect risk. Maternal serum screening (with or without nuchal translucency) provides a risk estimate for both aneuploidy and NTDs, and elevated AFP is the marker of open NTDs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Carrier screening assesses parental carrier status for conditions such as CF and SMA, not NTD risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CVS is used to confirm a positive aneuploidy screen; a low-risk cfDNA result does not require CVS, and CVS is not the NTD assessment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: cfDNA has high sensitivity and specificity for common aneuploidies, not for neural tube defects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NTDs can be assessed prenatally, for example by serum AFP screening or amniotic fluid AFP.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman, gravida 1, at 9 weeks' gestation presents with vaginal bleeding and cramping. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an intrauterine embryo with no cardiac activity. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this pregnancy loss?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent amniotic fluid from renal agenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Structural weakness of the cervical tissue

explanation.summary: Chromosomal abnormalities are the most common cause of spontaneous abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spontaneous abortion is loss of a pregnancy before 20 weeks. Chromosomal abnormalities are its most common cause, and their frequency rises with maternal age because oocytes, present since birth, accumulate mutations with aging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oligohydramnios from renal agenesis is a later-pregnancy problem, not the usual cause of early loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ultrasound shows an intrauterine embryo, so this is not an ectopic pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Placental abruption is typically a third-trimester complication, not a cause of 9-week loss.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical insufficiency causes painless dilation and second-trimester loss, not first-trimester embryonic demise.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has lower abdominal pain and a positive hCG test 7 weeks after her last menstrual period. Transvaginal ultrasound shows no intrauterine gestational sac. Which of the following is the most likely site of implantation?

explanation.summary: Most ectopic pregnancies implant in the ampulla of the uterine tube.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ampulla is the most common site of fertilization, and tubal scarring or adhesions there impede embryo transport, so it is the most common site of ectopic implantation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Abdominal implantation can occur but is far less common than tubal implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ampulla, not the isthmus, is the most common tubal site.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pouch of Douglas is a possible but uncommon ectopic site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tube (ampulla) is the most common location, not the ovary.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation has mild pelvic pain. Blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg and pulse is 80/min. Transvaginal ultrasound shows a small, intact gestation in the right uterine tube with no free fluid. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

explanation.summary: Stable patients with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy are preferentially treated with methotrexate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Methotrexate is preferred for a hemodynamically stable patient with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy; the tissue is then gradually absorbed or expelled. Surgery is reserved for rupture, significant hemorrhage, or instability.

whyWrongByChoice.A: D&C removes intrauterine tissue and cannot reach a tubal pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgery is required for rupture, hemorrhage, or instability, none of which is present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate is used before 32 weeks in preterm labor for fetal neuroprotection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This regimen evacuates the uterus in spontaneous abortion; it does not treat a tubal gestation.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation has regular uterine contractions, and her cervix is 4 cm dilated. She is given intramuscular betamethasone. Which of the following best describes how this drug benefits the newborn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks calcium entry into myometrial smooth muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the myometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protects the neonatal brain against cerebral palsy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relaxes uterine smooth muscle through beta-2 receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates surfactant release by type 2 alveolar cells

explanation.summary: Antenatal corticosteroids cross the placenta and accelerate fetal lung maturity by stimulating surfactant production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Betamethasone or dexamethasone crosses the placenta into the fetal circulation and stimulates type 2 alveolar cells to produce surfactant, reducing the severity of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is nifedipine's tocolytic mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is indomethacin's tocolytic mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate, not a corticosteroid, is given before 32 weeks to help prevent cerebral palsy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That is terbutaline's tocolytic mechanism, not the corticosteroid's benefit.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 29 weeks' gestation is in preterm labor. She receives betamethasone and is also started on intravenous magnesium sulfate. Which of the following is the main purpose of the magnesium sulfate in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accelerate surfactant production in the fetal lungs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the risk of cerebral palsy in the newborn

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prevent early closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reverse the cervical dilation already present

explanation.summary: Before 32 weeks, magnesium sulfate is given to help prevent cerebral palsy in the premature newborn.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cerebral palsy is a known complication of extreme prematurity. Magnesium sulfate given before 32 weeks helps prevent it, complementing corticosteroids, which address lung immaturity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is the role of the corticosteroid she already received.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Premature ductal closure is an NSAID adverse effect; magnesium is not given to prevent it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No listed agent reverses cervical dilation; true labor may not be haltable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infection is treated with antibiotics; magnesium sulfate is given for neuroprotection.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has been receiving a tocolytic for several days for recurrent preterm contractions. Ultrasound now shows markedly reduced amniotic fluid, and fetal echocardiography shows narrowing of the ductus arteriosus. Which of the following agents is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: NSAID tocolytics used for long periods or after 32 weeks can cause premature ductus closure and low amniotic fluid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Indomethacin decreases prostaglandin production. Because prostaglandins keep the ductus arteriosus open, prolonged use or use after 32 weeks can cause premature ductal closure and low amniotic fluid levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Betamethasone is a corticosteroid for fetal lung maturity, not a tocolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate is given before 32 weeks for fetal neuroprotection, not linked here to ductal closure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine, a calcium channel blocker, characteristically causes low blood pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Terbutaline's adverse effects are tachycardia and hyperglycemia.

questions.stem: A newborn delivered at 35 weeks has a flattened face, limb deformities, and severe respiratory difficulty. Prenatal ultrasound had shown almost no fluid around the fetus from early in the third trimester, with intact membranes. Which of the following fetal abnormalities most likely caused these findings?

explanation.summary: Oligohydramnios from absent fetal urine production causes compression deformities known as Potter sequence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amniotic fluid is largely fetal urine. Renal agenesis prevents urine production, causing oligohydramnios, and longstanding compression produces the deformities of Potter sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anencephaly impairs swallowing and is associated with polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A bilobed placenta is a cause of vasa previa, not of absent amniotic fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duodenal atresia prevents removal of fluid, producing polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired fetal swallowing causes polyhydramnios, not oligohydramnios.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has sudden bright red vaginal bleeding that began while she was resting. She has no pain or contractions. The uterus is soft and nontender, membranes are intact, and the fetal heart rate is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Painless third-trimester bleeding without warning is the classic presentation of placenta previa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Placenta previa, placental tissue over or near the cervical os, classically causes painless bleeding without warning after 20 weeks. Abruption instead causes painful bleeding with uterine tenderness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical insufficiency presents with painless cervical dilation, not heavy bright red bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abruption presents with pain, contractions, and uterine tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Preterm labor requires contractions with cervical change; she has no contractions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasa previa bleeds at membrane rupture with fetal bradycardia; membranes are intact and heart rate normal.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with chronic hypertension at 35 weeks' gestation presents with abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding, and a rigid, tender uterus. Two hours later, blood oozes from her intravenous sites and her platelet count is falling. Which of the following best explains the oozing?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the uterus to contract

explanation.summary: Complete placental abruption can be complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Painful bleeding with a tender uterus in a hypertensive patient indicates placental abruption. Disseminated intravascular coagulation can occur with complete abruption, producing diffuse bleeding such as oozing from IV sites.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Uterine atony causes postpartum hemorrhage, not diffuse coagulopathic oozing before delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal-vessel bleeding (vasa previa) would not cause maternal IV-site oozing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine causes low blood pressure, not a consumptive bleeding disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retained tissue after early pregnancy loss causes uterine bleeding or infection.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 39 weeks' gestation is in early labor. Her membranes rupture spontaneously, followed immediately by painless vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart rate abruptly falls to 80/min. Her vital signs are normal, and a prior ultrasound noted a velamentous cord insertion. Which of the following is the most likely source of the bleeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cervical vessels torn during early dilation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maternal decidual vessels behind a separated placenta

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maternal placental vessels overlying the os

choices.label: D
choices.text: Umbilical vessels running across the internal os

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterine vessels from a ruptured uterine tube

explanation.summary: Vasa previa bleeding comes from exposed fetal vessels, so it causes fetal distress while the mother remains stable.
explanation.whyCorrect: In vasa previa, fetal vessels lie over the internal cervical os, often from a velamentous cord. Membrane rupture tears these vessels, causing painless bleeding that is fetal blood, hence the fetal bradycardia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical change does not explain fetal bradycardia right after rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is placental abruption, which is typically painful with uterine tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That is placenta previa, where bleeding is maternal and not triggered by membrane rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tubal rupture is an early ectopic pregnancy event, not a term labor finding.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy has an ultrasound at 22 weeks. One twin is small with signs of poor organ perfusion; the other is larger with cardiomegaly and signs of heart failure. Which of the following best explains the discordance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chromosomal abnormality affecting only the smaller twin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Separate placentas with unequal sites of implantation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Umbilical cord entanglement within a single amniotic sac

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unequal flow across placental vascular connections

explanation.summary: Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome arises only in monochorionic twins from abnormal vascular connections in the shared placenta.
explanation.whyCorrect: In TTTS, abnormal connections within a single placenta create unequal blood flow: the donor twin develops growth restriction and hypoperfusion, and the recipient develops volume overload and heart failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A karyotype problem would not explain heart failure in the larger co-twin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Maternal diabetes causes polyhydramnios, not donor-recipient discordance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Separate placentas describe dichorionic twins, which cannot develop TTTS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cord entanglement complicates monoamniotic twins; these twins are diamniotic.

questions.stem: Ultrasound at 30 weeks' gestation shows an excess of amniotic fluid. After delivery, the newborn drools excessively, and a feeding tube cannot be passed into the stomach. Which of the following best explains the prenatal fluid abnormality?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leakage through a defect in the amniotic sac

explanation.summary: Conditions that block fetal swallowing, such as esophageal atresia, cause polyhydramnios.
explanation.whyCorrect: The newborn has esophageal atresia. Because the fetus normally removes amniotic fluid by swallowing, obstruction of swallowing leaves excess fluid, producing polyhydramnios.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Maternal diabetes causes polyhydramnios by fetal polyuria, but this newborn has esophageal atresia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Obstructed urine flow reduces fluid, causing oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leakage reduces fluid, causing oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Placental insufficiency causes growth restriction, not excess fluid.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 17 weeks' gestation, dated by a first-trimester ultrasound, requests termination of pregnancy. She has no medical conditions and no prior uterine surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate method at this gestational age?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mifepristone given as a single agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Misoprostol given as a single agent

explanation.summary: Dilation and evacuation is the method used for abortion beyond the first trimester, up to 24 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture's timing table limits medical abortion to about 10 weeks (FDA) or 12 weeks (WHO) and manual vacuum aspiration to 10-14 weeks. Dilation and evacuation, which uses cervical dilation plus instruments and suction to empty the uterus, can be performed up to 24 weeks, making it the appropriate choice at 17 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Manual vacuum aspiration is used up to about 10-14 weeks, so 17 weeks is beyond its range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The combined medical regimen is used up to 10 weeks (FDA) or 12 weeks (WHO).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mifepristone is used in combination with misoprostol in early pregnancy, not alone in the second trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Misoprostol alone is a first-trimester option (up to 10 weeks) when mifepristone is unavailable.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation chooses medical abortion and takes mifepristone in the clinic, with a second medication to be taken at home. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the drug taken in the clinic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks estrogen receptors in the endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks progesterone needed to sustain the pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibits folate metabolism in the trophoblast

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulates uterine smooth muscle to contract

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppresses pituitary release of luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: Mifepristone blocks the progesterone that supports the conceptus during pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the lecture's table, mifepristone blocks the progesterone needed to support the conceptus during pregnancy. It is used up to 10 weeks in combination with misoprostol, which then causes uterine contractions that expel the conceptus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mifepristone acts on progesterone, not estrogen, signaling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lecture does not describe an antifolate mechanism for either abortion medication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inducing uterine contractions to expel the conceptus is the action of misoprostol, the second drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mifepristone does not act by suppressing pituitary gonadotropins.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 8 weeks' gestation elects medical abortion. The clinic where she is seen has no supply of mifepristone. Which of the following regimens is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: When mifepristone is unavailable, misoprostol can be used alone for medical abortion up to 10 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Medical abortion uses mifepristone plus misoprostol, but the lecture notes that misoprostol can be used alone when mifepristone is not available. At 8 weeks she is within the medical-abortion window, and misoprostol causes uterine contractions that expel the conceptus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uterotonics like this are used for bleeding; the lecture's alternative regimen is misoprostol alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxytocin is not described as a medical abortion regimen in early pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone supports the conceptus; blocking it (not giving it) is the goal of mifepristone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antifibrinolytics are used to treat hemorrhage, not to induce abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman took mifepristone and then misoprostol at 8 weeks' gestation 5 days ago. For the past 3 hours she has soaked more than one pad per hour, with cramping. Blood pressure is 112/70 mm Hg and pulse is 98/min. After assessing her hemodynamic status, which of the following evaluations is most important?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abdominal CT to look for bowel injury

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood cultures for suspected septic endometritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultrasound for retained products of conception

explanation.summary: Hemorrhage after medical abortion should prompt evaluation for incomplete abortion (retained products of conception).
explanation.whyCorrect: Filling a pad an hour warrants contact and evaluation. The lecture states that hemorrhage after a medical abortion should prompt evaluation for incomplete abortion or retained products of conception, along with possible evaluation for an underlying bleeding disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Visceral injury is a concern with surgical perforation, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: She has no fever, discharge, or other signs of infection; bleeding is the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tubal patency is irrelevant to acute bleeding after abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uterine perforation is a rare complication of surgical, not medical, abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman underwent vacuum aspiration at 9 weeks' gestation 4 days ago. She now has a temperature of 38.6 C (101.5 F), lower abdominal pain, uterine tenderness, and a foul-smelling cervical discharge. Leukocyte count is 16,000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and appropriate management?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uterine atony treated with uterotonic drugs

explanation.summary: Fever, pelvic pain, leukocytosis, and foul discharge after surgical abortion indicate endometritis requiring antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists fever, abdominal or pelvic pain, leukocytosis, and foul-smelling vaginal or cervical discharge as the signs of infection (endometritis) after surgical abortion. Patients with infection require antibiotic treatment, and severe infection may require hospitalization. Infection is uncommon (<1%) when prophylaxis is used.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fever, leukocytosis, and foul discharge are not expected post-procedure findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She had a surgical procedure, and misoprostol fever is low-grade without other symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Atony causes hemorrhage, not fever with foul discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Perforation presents with concern for hemorrhage or organ injury, not purulent discharge with leukocytosis.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation chooses medical abortion with mifepristone and misoprostol. She asks which antibiotic she should take beforehand to prevent infection. According to ACOG, which of the following is the most appropriate response?

explanation.summary: ACOG does not recommend antibiotic prophylaxis before medical abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: According to ACOG, antibiotics are not necessary before medical abortion. By contrast, ACOG and WHO recommend antibiotic prophylaxis (doxycycline, azithromycin, or metronidazole) for surgical abortion, alongside sterile technique.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is used for surgical abortion prophylaxis, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No antibiotic prophylaxis is recommended for medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is a prophylactic option for surgical abortion, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole is a surgical prophylaxis option; medical abortion does not require antibiotics.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has an uncomplicated vacuum aspiration at 8 weeks' gestation. She wants a hormonal implant to prevent future pregnancy and has no contraindications. When is the most appropriate time to place the implant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: After 3 months of using condoms alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: After a negative pregnancy test in 4 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: After her first menstrual period returns

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immediately, at the time of the abortion

explanation.summary: Most contraceptive methods, including implants, can be started immediately after abortion if medically eligible and desired.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that most contraceptive methods after abortion should be initiated immediately if the patient is medically eligible and it aligns with her goals, including hormonal implants, oral contraceptives, IUDs, condoms, emergency contraception, and cervical caps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No waiting period is recommended before starting a hormonal method.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no need to delay contraception for a confirmatory test in an eligible patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting for menses is unnecessary; most methods can start immediately if eligible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Routine in-person follow-up is not required, and delay leaves her unprotected.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: Before performing a surgical abortion, a physician explains to the patient how the procedure is done and its risks. To complete the informed consent process, which of the following must also be discussed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her detailed reasons for seeking abortion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her partner's written agreement to proceed

choices.label: D
choices.text: The physician's personal views on abortion

choices.label: E
choices.text: The worldwide legal status of abortion

explanation.summary: Informed consent covers how the procedure is done, its risks, its benefits, and the available alternatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that obtaining informed consent involves educating patients on how the procedure is done, its risks and benefits, and available alternatives, so that the patient fully understands the procedure before giving permission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Patients do not have to justify their decision to give informed consent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Consent is the patient's own decision; a partner's agreement is not an element.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Counseling should be nonjudgmental; personal views are not part of consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Global legal status is not an element of informed consent for her procedure.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation is deciding whether to continue her pregnancy. She asks how the risk of death from abortion compares with the risk of death from continuing a pregnancy. According to CDC data, which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abortion carries far lower risk, constant across gestation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abortion carries far lower risk, rising with gestational age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Abortion carries higher risk, falling with gestational age

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continued pregnancy carries lower risk before 12 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: The two carry similar risk, about 1 per 100,000 each

explanation.summary: Abortion mortality (0.3-1 per 100,000) is far lower than that of continued pregnancy (17.9 per 100,000) and rises with gestational age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the CDC figures in the lecture, the risk of death from abortion is 0.3-1 per 100,000, increasing with gestational age, whereas the risk of death from a continued pregnancy is 17.9 per 100,000. Rates vary by geography, age, race and ethnicity, and underlying medical conditions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture states abortion mortality increases with increasing gestational age.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abortion mortality (0.3-1/100,000) is far below that of continued pregnancy (17.9/100,000) and rises with gestation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Abortion is safer than continued pregnancy; there is no early-gestation reversal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Continued pregnancy carries about 17.9 deaths per 100,000, far higher than abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A public health team compares countries that have highly restrictive abortion laws with countries that provide broad legal access. Which of the following outcomes is most consistently observed in the countries with highly restrictive laws?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A higher proportion of unsafe abortions

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lower rate of abortion-related hemorrhage

explanation.summary: Highly restrictive abortion laws are associated with a significantly higher proportion of unsafe abortions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that patients usually find a way to induce an abortion whether or not it is legal, and that in countries with highly restrictive laws the proportion of unsafe abortions is significantly higher, endangering patients' health and lives.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Unsafe abortion raises, not lowers, the risk of hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Restriction does not stop patients from seeking to end pregnancies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sepsis is a serious complication of unsafe abortion, which is more common under restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Evidence suggests patients usually find a way to induce abortion whether or not it is legal.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A physician is counseling a 19-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation who has decided to have an abortion. Which of the following statements by the physician best reflects recommended counseling practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Before we proceed, let me share my own opinion."

choices.label: B
choices.text: "Have you thought about how your family will react?"

choices.label: C
choices.text: "I understand this is an unwanted pregnancy for you."

choices.label: D
choices.text: "Let's go over each option and what to expect with it."

choices.label: E
choices.text: "Since this pregnancy was unplanned, let's review options."

explanation.summary: Abortion counseling should use clear, objective, noninflammatory language that avoids labels such as 'unplanned' or 'unwanted.'
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture's counseling guidelines are to avoid judgment, provide clear accurate information, use noninflammatory language (avoiding qualifiers like 'unplanned' or 'unwanted'), provide resources, and create a safe space. Offering to review each option and what to expect does this.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clinicians should avoid judgment and maintain objectivity to respect autonomy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This question implies judgment rather than objective, supportive counseling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Calling the pregnancy 'unwanted' is inflammatory language the lecture advises against.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Qualifiers such as 'unplanned' should be avoided when describing the pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation takes mifepristone and, 1 day later, misoprostol. Six hours after the misoprostol dose, her temperature is 37.9 C (100.2 F). She has cramping similar to menses, no uterine tenderness, and no abnormal discharge. Leukocyte count is normal. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for her temperature?

explanation.summary: Up to half of patients given misoprostol have a low-grade fever without other symptoms; infection after medical abortion is rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that infection after medical abortion is rare, although half of patients given misoprostol may have low-grade fevers without other symptoms. Her isolated low-grade fever with normal leukocyte count and no tenderness or discharge fits this expected drug effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture attributes post-medication low-grade fever to misoprostol, not mifepristone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sepsis would not present as an isolated low-grade temperature with normal labs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometritis would bring pelvic tenderness, leukocytosis, or foul discharge, all absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Perforation is a complication of surgical abortion, not medical abortion.
